To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the early responses of rice to anaerobiosis are mainly due to the enhancement of the expression of a few genes, and that the expression of some of these genes is tissue specific.

(a) the anaerobiosis-mediated early changes in the protein synthesis in rice roots and coleoptile are mainly due to the enhancement of the expression of specific mRNA species, (b) these mRNA species are differentially regulated during the first hours in both rice coleoptiles and rice roots, and (c) a rapid decrease of mRNA species coding for polypeptide of 38 kDa was observed in both organs.

rice roots and coleoptile exhibit a rapid transcriptional and translatalional response to anaerobiosis, which is characterized by the enhancement of the expression of several genes and the down regulation of others.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying the adaptation to hypoxia of the two major organs of rice, the root and the shoot.
the early transcriptional and post-transcriptional changes that occur in rice roots and coleoptile tissues during the first hours after anaerobiosis.
the study of the transcriptional and the translational changes that occur in rice organs during anoxia, in particular during the first hours after oxygen deprivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anaerobic response in rice coleoptiles and rice roots is characterized by a rapid and transient induction of a specific set of genes coding for proteins with a wide range of molecular weights.

anaerobic stress in rice roots and coleoptile induces an early and rapid transcriptional and translatal response, and that the early anaerobiosis-induced changes in gene expression are organ specific.

anaerobic conditions induce a rapid and specific increase in the level(s) of the mRNA(s) coding for polypeptide(s) with molecular weight(s) of 67–54 and 34 and a rapid and specific decrease in the level of mRNA(s) coding a polypeptide with molecular weight of 38.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

rice coleoptiles and rice roots respond to anaerobiosis by activating specific transcriptional and translateral programs, which include a reduction in the level in mRNAs coding polypeptides of molecular weights of 38 kDa and the synthesis of polypptides of molecular weights 13–16 and 34 kDa, respectively.

the anaerobic induction of specific mRNAs coding polypeptides with molecular weights of approximately 67–62 kD, 54, 34 and 13–16 kDa is one of the earliest events in rice coleoptiles and in rice roots during anoxia.

the early anaerobic responses in rice roots and coleoptilies are characterized by a rapid enhancement of the synthesis (and/or accumulation) of specific proteins, which is accompanied by a parallel increase in the corresponding mRNA levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early anaerobic response is characterized by the induction of specific transcriptional and translatorial changes that are common to both rice roots and coleoptile.
anaerobiosis triggers early changes at the transcriptional and/or translational levels in rice organs.

the early transcriptional and post-transcriptional changes in rice roots and coleoptilies are very similar, and that they occur in both organs within 1h of anaerobiosis, suggesting that the early response to anaerobiosis in rice roots and in coleoptiles are highly conserved.
